papers.scope_note: Primary experimental study of negative-tone n-butyltin-oxo cage resists with hydroxide, acetate and malonate counterions, including EUV open-frame contrast and interference lithography.

papers.title: Ti, Zr, and Hf-based molecular hybrid materials as EUV photoresists
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Experimental comparison of molecular Ti-, Zr-, and Hf-oxo methacrylate EUV resists, including negative-tone patterning of ZrMc and HfMc and unsuccessful solubility contrast for TiMc.

papers.title: Surface characterization of tin-based inorganic EUV resists
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Experimental study of the negative-tone tin-oxo cluster resist β-NaSn13, comparing X-ray-induced insolubilization in UHV and oxygen and investigating annealing chemistry. Designed for EUV use, but the reported contrast experiments use Al Kα X-rays rather than EUV lithography.

papers.title: Zinc-based metal oxoclusters: Towards enhanced EUV absorptivity
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Experimental study of a tetrameric Zn-oxo, mixed-carboxylate photoresist, including EUV developer screening, PEB effects, batch-specific patterning and stability. The reported bulk formula is an average composition, not an atomically resolved coated-film structure.

papers.title: The role of the organic shell in hybrid molecular materials for EUV lithography
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Experimental study of methacrylate-shell-doped zirconium metal-oxo EUV resists, with a qualitative hafnium analogue comparison. Includes negative-tone contrast measurements, dense-line patterning, pillar patterning, and calculated EUV absorption.

papers.title: All New Nickel Based Metal Core Organic Cluster (MCOC) Resist for N7+Node Patterning
papers.journal: ADVANCES IN PATTERNING MATERIALS AND PROCESSES XXXVII
papers.scope_note: Original experimental study of a nickel–DMA metal-organic cluster resist with proposed Ni–O bonding, tested by helium-ion and electron-beam lithography. Atomic cluster structure is unresolved; EUV use is prospective rather than demonstrated.

papers.title: Influence of the anion in tin-based EUV photoresists properties
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Direct EUV lithography study of two butyl-Sn12 oxo-hydroxo cage salts with different counterions; Tin(OAc)2 is an experimentally measured photodegradation reference, without a reported lithographic performance condition here.

papers.title: Study on resist performance of inorganic-organic resist materials for EUV and EB lithography
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Experimental comparison of methacrylic-acid-derived Ti-, Zr-, and Hf-based metal-oxo resists using EUV sensitivity measurements, EB sensitivity and patterning experiments, and annealing-dependent RIE tests.

papers.title: Electron beam lithography validation of a new resist development for ultrafine patterns
papers.journal: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
papers.scope_note: Experimental lithography study of two negative-tone metal oxide resists, P28 MOR and P14 MOR. Metal identity, molecular composition and discrete metal-oxo cluster structure are not established in the supplied evidence.

papers.title: Electronics of molecular nanoclusters
papers.scope_note: The paper investigates molecular nanoclusters as single-electron tunneling components, not photoresists (MAIN:p1–MAIN:p11). Conventional EBL fabricates electrodes before cluster-film deposition; the reported 0–20 nm electrode gaps are not cluster-resist patterning performance (MAIN:p10).

papers.title: Coulomb-blockade dominated transport in patterned gold-cluster structures
papers.journal: JAPANESE JOURNAL OF APPLIED PHYSICS PART 1-REGULAR PAPERS BRIEF COMMUNICATIONS & REVIEW PAPERS
papers.scope_note: Ligand-stabilized gold clusters are directly patterned as a negative-tone electron-beam-sensitive material. This is a related metal-organic cluster lithography study focused on electrical transport, not a metal-oxo or EUV resist study.

papers.title: Metal-based extreme ultraviolet photoresist
papers.scope_note: Review of metal-oxo clusters, metal-oxide nanoparticles and molecular/polymeric metal-organic resists. Extracted results are literature comparisons, not experiments performed in this review; mechanism-only discussions and unrelated introductory citations are not expanded into resist-performance records.

papers.title: Performance and mechanism of novel antimony oxo cluster photoresist
papers.scope_note: Original study of two crystallographically characterized antimony oxo clusters. Sb4O-1 is a solubility comparator; condition-specific negative-tone EBL performance is reported for Sb4O-2.

papers.title: A facile size-control method of CdS nanoparticles in-situ synthesized in polymer matrix by adjusting ratio of acidic acid with metallic complex in acrylate photoresist resin
papers.scope_note: Metal-containing, non-cluster acrylate photoresist formulations are photopolymerized to support in situ CdS nanoparticle formation. The study reports formulation and curing conditions with optical functionality, but no metal-oxo cluster resist or condition-specific lithographic performance.

papers.title: Photoreactions of tin oxo cages, model EUV photoresists
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Direct study of tin oxo cage model EUV photoresists, focused on TinOAc DUV photochemistry in solution and thin films. Reported exposure records are photochemical tests, not lithographic dose-to-size or resolution demonstrations.

papers.title: Photo-induced fragmentation of a Tin-oxo cage compound
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Mechanistic study of an n-butyl tin-oxo cage photoresist using isolated gas-phase ions and solution absorption measurements. No condition-specific film lithography is performed; the EUV tone and absorption statements are prior-literature context.

papers.title: Dual-tone application of a tin-oxo cage photoresist under E-beam and EUV exposure
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Direct experimental study of hydroxide-counterion tin-oxo cage TinOH as a dual-tone EUV and electron-beam photoresist.

papers.title: Metal Organic Cluster Photoresists for EUV Lithography
papers.journal: JOURNAL OF PHOTOPOLYMER SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
papers.scope_note: Directly reports zirconium and zinc metal-organic cluster photoresists, with a zirconium oxide nanoparticle comparator. Figures 1–5 reproduce prior literature results; Figure 6 reports the underlayer study without a reproduction attribution.

papers.title: Xuv induced bleaching of a tin oxo cage photoresist studied by high harmonic absorption spectroscopy
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Direct study of XUV-induced bleaching in the TinOH metal-oxo cage photoresist, not a lithographic patterning demonstration. EUV absorption and undisclosed Inpria resist Dill parameters are retained as literature comparisons.

papers.title: Photon-induced fragmentation of zinc-based oxoclusters for euv lithography applications
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Mechanistic study of zinc-oxo cluster EUV photoresist materials using gas-phase cation photofragmentation. The reviewed paper provides no condition-specific lithography performance records; the reported EUV absorption is retained as prior-work context.

papers.title: Chemical Mechanisms of Metal-Based Extreme Ultraviolet Resists
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Mechanistic review of metal-oxo clusters with acrylate ligands and organotin-oxo cages. Retained results are literature comparisons, not new experiments; gas-phase photochemistry and passing mentions of other precursors are not treated as lithography performance records.

papers.title: Influence of Counteranions on the Performance of Tin-based EUV Photoresists
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Original study of three counterion-modified tin-oxo-hydroxo cage EUV resists, with interference-lithography performance and in-situ irradiation chemistry.

papers.title: Electron Generation in Tin-oxo Cage Extreme Ultraviolet Photoresists
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Direct study of an n-butyltin-oxo cage photoresist using TEY spectroscopy across 5–150 eV. It reports electron-generation and radiation-response properties, not condition-specific lithographic patterning performance.

papers.title: Evaluation of Inorganic-organic Hybrid Resist Materials with Ultrafast Coherent High Harmonic Generation (HHG) EUV System Developed in QST
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: This study evaluates Zr-based and Hf-based metal-oxo cluster negative-tone resists using HHG EUV, reporting line formation and sensitivity curves.

papers.title: Effect of Organic Ligand Structure on Resist Performance of Inorganic-Organic Hybrid Resist Materials for EB and EUV Lithography
papers.journal: Journal of Photopolymer Science and Technology
papers.scope_note: Direct EB and EUV evaluation of salicylic-acid-ligated Zr-based oxo cluster resist, with etching experiments and selected prior-study ligand comparisons.

papers.title: Effect of Free Radicals on Irradiation Chemistry of a Double-Coordination Organotin (Sn4) Photoresist by Adjusting Alkyl Ligands
papers.scope_note: Original study of two Sn4 tin-oxo/organotin cluster photoresists, including negative-tone EBL and EUV patterning, benzoquinone-dependent behavior, film roughness, thermal stability and etching. Background citations were not extracted as this study's experiments.

papers.title: Synthesis, Characterization , and Radiation Chemistry of Fluorine-Rich Zr-Sn-oxo Clusters
papers.scope_note: Primary study of atomically resolved Zr6Sn4-oxo cluster precursors SnOC-3, SnOC-4 and SnOC-5 as single-component EBL resists. EUV suitability is discussed, but no direct EUV lithography experiment is reported; SnOC-6 and SnOC-7 are mechanistic solubility controls.

papers.title: Zirconium-Oxo Clusters for High-Resolution Lithography : Influence of the Organic-Ligand Coordination Mode
papers.scope_note: Original experimental study of three methacrylate-coordinated Zr6 cluster photoresists evaluated by EBL and EUVL, with DUV mechanistic studies and plasma-etch testing.

papers.title: Opening the Coordination Sphere of Organotin Oxo Clusters Through Vanadium Doping: From Precise Ligands Engineering to Tunable Lithography Reactivity
papers.scope_note: Original experimental study of crystallographically characterized Sn8V2 organotin-oxo clusters used as negative-tone electron-beam resists. EUV is a proposed application, not an exposure experiment reported here; series entries denote separately prepared materials, not mixtures.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Metal-Oxide-Based Photoresists for EUV Lithography
papers.scope_note: Review of metal-oxo cluster, metal-oxide nanoparticle and related hybrid resists. Extracted results are literature comparisons, not experiments performed in this review; unrelated nanoparticle synthesis and sensor performance are excluded.

papers.title: Ligand Functionality-Dependent Performance of Organotin Carboxylate Resists
papers.scope_note: Direct experimental DUV study of two molecular organotin carboxylate resists, not preformed metal-oxo clusters. Metal-oxo network formation is a proposed exposure mechanism; no EUV or EBL performance experiments are reported.

papers.title: Study on radical dianions of carboxylates used as ligands of metal oxide nanocluster resists
papers.scope_note: This study investigates aqueous free carboxylic acids/carboxylates by pulse radiolysis as models of resist ligand chemistry, not metal-oxo or metal-organic resist materials or films (MAIN:p2–MAIN:p3, MAIN:p11). The electron irradiation and reaction kinetics are not lithography performance measurements; the qualitative literature sensitivity comparison does not identify a condition-specific resist result.

papers.title: Sensitization mechanism of metal oxide nanocluster resists with carboxylic acid ligands
papers.scope_note: Mechanistic study of free carboxylic acid solutions as models for metal oxide nanocluster resist ligands, not an experimental study of coated metal-containing resists. No identifiable metal-containing material with condition-specific lithography performance was tested; solution radiolysis results are not extracted as resist performance.

papers.title: A study on the resist performance of inorganic-organic resist materials for EUV and electron-beam lithography
papers.scope_note: Experimental study of Ti-, Zr-, and Hf-based metal-oxo cluster resists with MAA ligands, including EUV and EBL sensitivity, EBL patterning, and etch durability.

papers.title: Effect of organic ligand and metal nanocluster core structure on resist performance of inorganic-organic hybrid resist materials for EUV and EB lithography
papers.journal: Japanese Journal of Applied Physics Part 1 Regular Papers and Short Notes and Review Papers
papers.scope_note: Original experimental study of twelve sol–gel-derived Hf-, Zr- and Ti-based oxo-cluster resists with four carboxylate ligands, including EBL sensitivity/patterning and EUV sensitivity for Hf–TiA and Zr–TiA. Atomically defined cluster structures and their retention in coated films are not established.

papers.title: Research Progress and Prospects of Extreme Ultraviolet Photoresists
papers.journal: Zhongguo Jiguang Chinese Journal of Lasers
papers.scope_note: Review of EUV photoresists, including metal-organic molecules, metal oxide nanoparticles and metal oxo clusters. Extraction prioritizes these metal-containing systems; all results are literature comparisons, including the authors' summaries of their previously published work.

papers.title: Pulse radiolysis of carboxylic acids used as ligands of metal oxide nanocluster resists
papers.scope_note: This study examines pulse radiolysis of free carboxylic acids in solution as models for metal oxide nanocluster resist ligands, not metal-containing resist materials or patterned films (MAIN:p2–MAIN:p7). Solution-phase reaction constants and radical-ion stability do not establish lithographic performance or resist-film stability.

papers.title: THE COORDINATION CHEMISTRY OF LOW VALENT SILICON
papers.scope_note: This coordination-chemistry review covers low-valent silicon complexes, not metal-oxo or metal-organic photoresist performance (MAIN:p2, MAIN:p3). Polysilane photoresists are mentioned only as an application with literature citations (MAIN:p4, MAIN:p42, MAIN:p43); the reported complex photochemistry is not a lithography experiment.

coverage_issues.note: MAIN:p1–MAIN:p10 report thermally initiated cluster cross-linking of PMMA, swelling, thermal degradation and electrical properties, not resist exposure or patterning. Lithographic dose, resolution, tone, contrast, LER/LWR, film thickness, substrate, development and lithographic bake conditions are absent.
No supplementary files were supplied or reviewed; review was limited to the ten supplied article page images.

No radiation-patterned resist experiments, exposure doses, development conditions, tone, resist contrast or LER/LWR are reported. Imprinted MoS2 dimensions and thermal-processing conditions are not photoresist performance.
Supplied text covers MAIN:p1–p9 and SI1:p1–p16; visual review is limited to MAIN:p1–p6, MAIN:p8 and SI1:p11. Other figure pixels were not supplied or reviewed.
Only eight selected SI images were supplied and visually reviewed; publisher figures and other SI image pixels were unavailable. DOCX page layout was not preserved.

Sn4-TF's complete formula and exact fluorinated aryl ligand substitution are not established by the supplied readable evidence. Sn4-2F crystallography establishes the precursor structure, not retention of discrete clusters in coated or exposed films; counterions are not identified.

PAB/PEB conditions, development duration, rinsing, EUV numerical aperture and precise substrate identity for individual lithography results are absent. General coating uses polished wafers; no bake is inferred.

Table S2 image was not supplied, preventing condition-specific thickness verification beyond the general EBL thicknesses in MAIN:b31. NI2 identity and exact spin-speed assignment to individual results are unresolved.

coverage_issues.field: Developed thickness, thickness loss and EUV absorption
coverage_issues.note: No explicit numerical developed thickness, thickness loss or material-specific EUV absorption coefficient is given in readable text or labels. Normalized thickness curves were not digitized.
Lacerm software is identified, but sigma convention, sampling length and measurement protocol are unspecified; X labels are not numerical LER values.
Images for Sn4-2F developer-specific contrast, pre-irradiation contrast series and EUV contrast curves were not supplied. Only corresponding explicit MAIN values were extracted.
MAIN:b8 reports 8 and 34 nm CDs, while the S9 caption lists 9 and 21 nC/cm exposures without resolving which dose produced each CD.

coverage_issues.field: SEM montage subseries and mesh patterns
coverage_issues.note: S17/S18 captions identify developer groups but do not specify the different line-array geometries within each group. Mesh images provide line-dose labels without explicit numerical CD or LER.

coverage_issues.field: AFM height scales and unlabeled plot
coverage_issues.note: S24 color-scale maxima of 18.6, 16.1 and 20.9 nm are not identified as film thickness or roughness. S15 lacks readable numerical axes in the supplied image and yields no precise values.

MAIN:b12's approximate family resolutions are not individual dose-paired endpoints; S13 instead supplies explicit developer-specific CDs, including 8 nm for 2-heptanone. S17/S18 contain apparent dose-label errors that are retained rather than silently corrected.
Only the five supplied embedded SI images were visually reviewed. Publisher figure pixels and all other SI figure pixels were unavailable; DOCX page layout was not preserved.

The cage assignment is supported by reported spectroscopy and a known framework, not crystallographic resolution supplied here. Amorphous films and proposed DHP interactions do not establish retention of an atomically defined precursor structure.

No material-specific EUV absorption coefficient, D50, numeric LWR, LER sigma convention, EUV development time or explicit EUV PEB condition is supplied. Developed residual thickness and development-induced thickness loss are generally not quantified.
The 100 nm Mixture A EBL dose and nanoscale transfer-pattern doses are unresolved. Overall EBL and EUV test ranges are not assigned as successful dose-to-size windows.
The 14 and 16 nm half-pitch panels in the first dose column say 70 mJ/cm2 while the header says 71 mJ/cm2. Empty cells do not establish either failure or untested conditions.
The 30 nm transfer pattern is half-pitch in SI methods and image but CD in its caption. The finest EUV pattern is 12 nm half-pitch in the SI image but described as 12 nm linewidth in main text.
Main text reports 13 nm linewidth at 91 mJ/cm2; the corresponding 28 nm-pitch SI panel labels 13.4 nm CD. These are retained as one condition rather than invented separate experiments.
No graph digitization was performed. Unlabeled contrast endpoints, exact modulus/hardness, intermediate UV linewidths and profile heights were not inferred from plots or unavailable figure pixels.
Mixture A contrast ranges are reported across series without individual mappings; grouped records preserve them. The DSBTOC 7-day numerical contrast is absent from supplied text.
Main text gives approximately 100–120 nm, whereas SI methods give approximately 100–130 nm.
The defined composition is DSBTOC:DHP = 1:0.1 by weight; the conclusion also calls this 10 wt.% DHP. The explicit component ratio is retained without treating it as 10% of total solids.
The author statement of roughly tenfold improvement is retained separately from measured rates of 0.21 and 4.1 nm/s. These descriptions are not silently equated.

Only the eight supplied SI images were visually reviewed; publisher figure pixels and other SI images were unavailable. DOCX page layout was not preserved, and adfm73157-sup-0002-DataFile.zip was not read.

Only BTOC has a reported single-crystal structure; this does not establish retained cage structure in coated films. N-TOC6/TOC6 structures are proposed from spectroscopy and mass evidence, and no complete original molecular formula is supplied in the reviewed text.
MAIN:b20 reports 58 mJ/cm2, whereas MAIN:b47 reports 55 mJ/cm2 for 18 nm patterns with 2.1 nm LER; retained as one contradictory result rather than separate experiments.
MAIN:b18–b19 specify 150 °C for 2 min; MAIN:b52 specifies 150 °C for 1 min.

coverage_issues.field: TEM specimen CD and process pairing
coverage_issues.note: MAIN:b21 reports 43 nm features, but SI1:image185_1 labels CD 42 nm, LER 6.7 nm and dose 1500 microC/cm2. The specimen's initial thickness, developer and bake conditions are not explicitly paired.

coverage_issues.field: Supercritical CO2 pattern size and pressure graphic
coverage_issues.note: MAIN:b22 reports 70 nm width, while SI1:image198_1 labels nominal 70 nm patterns and measured mean CD 77 nm. Text and caption state 20 MPa, but the plotted pressure marker appears inconsistent; no coordinate-derived pressure was extracted.
MAIN:b37 gives a 17 nm top layer and 26 nm total bilayer, then describes a supposedly identical-thickness control as 16 nm.
Patterning methods use FC-3283, while MAIN:b48 and SI1:b41 list FC-8283 among purchased materials; the method-specific FC-3283 designation is retained.

SI1:image257_1 visibly concerns reorganization length, contrary to adjacent S34 text about interaction radius; SI1:image261_1 visibly concerns interaction radius, contrary to adjacent S35 text about reorganization length.

No graph digitization was performed for support ratios, crosslinked-ligand counts, unlabeled contrast endpoints, mechanical-property magnitudes or spectral bars. Only explicit labels and textual values were retained.

coverage_issues.field: Core performance fields absent from reviewed evidence
coverage_issues.note: LER sigma convention, LWR, most developed thicknesses and quantitative exposure/development thickness losses are absent. Numerical EUV absorption coefficients, measured quantum yields, most pattern pitches and bilayer development time are also not reported.

The text identifies EUV generally as 13.5 nm but does not separately specify wavelength for each experiment; DCT location descriptions are not consistent across sections. DSBTOC PED-series PAB and concentration are not explicitly supplied, and 4% wt./vol. for baseline EBL differs from 4 wt.% for PED experiments.
No figure pixels or images were supplied; only text and captions were reviewed. The listed supplementary DOCX and crystallographic files were not acquired or reviewed.

Experimental film thickness, formulation concentrations, spin parameters, PAB, complete PEB schedules and development times are deferred to unavailable Tables S6, S7 and S11. The 60 °C EBL PEB is explicit, but optimized EUV processing values are unavailable.

EUV LER values are assigned to unavailable Figures S22–S24; no numerical LER or sigma/measurement definition is supplied in the reviewed text. No LWR values are reported there; AFM RMS roughness is retained separately.

coverage_issues.field: developed thickness, thickness loss and EUV contrast
coverage_issues.note: No explicit measured initial/developed thickness pair, thickness-loss value, EUV contrast or D50 is given in the supplied text; the optimized EUV height-retention claim is qualitative.

EBL 40/60 nC/cm line doses are paired only collectively with Sn2-4F's 10–12 nm CD range; high-resolution developers are unresolved. Optimized 10 mJ/cm2 EUV has no stated target CD and cannot inherit the baseline 22 nm CD.
Figure 4 captions specify 75 nm pitch, whereas methods report both 75 and 60 nm patterns. Material/dose assignments for the 60 nm-pitch patterns are unavailable.

Atomically resolved status refers to reported precursor SC-XRD, not independently reviewed crystallographic data. Coated films are described as amorphous, and retention of the discrete precursor architecture in films is not established by the supplied evidence.

D0 is called a fitted characteristic dose without an operational threshold definition. Cyclohexane D0 ≈ 2 µC/cm2 lies below the stated 3–147 µC/cm2 exposure series and is preserved without correction.

coverage_issues.field: etch selectivity orientation and per-material rates

For the extracted metal-containing systems, numerical PAB/PEB conditions, developer identity/time, substrates, formulation concentrations, beam energies, instrument settings, contrast, LER/LWR definitions and values, developed thickness, and thickness loss are generally absent. The review's general 13.5 nm EUV description was not assigned as a verified instrument condition to every record.

Most cluster labels give nuclearity rather than complete formulas, ligand inventories or counterions. Atomic precision is explicitly reported for the non-alkyl Sn cluster study, but retention of precursor structures in coated films is not established.
MAIN:p11 explicitly reports 10–40 mJ/cm2 for electron-beam lithography; the unit inconsistency is preserved without conversion or reassignment to EUV.

The 12 nm MAPDST-co-ADSM result is not assigned to one of three compositions. In12 functionalizations and three soluble Ti-Zr clusters have grouped performance statements without individual exposure conditions.
Ti-Zr cluster resolutions are not identified as half-pitch or linewidth; they remain unspecified rather than being reclassified.

No material-specific quantitative EUV absorption coefficients or etch rates are given for the extracted metal-containing systems. Ti-Zr etching and pattern-transfer investigations are mentioned without extractable performance values.

Hafnium oxo-methacrylate and Zr6O4(OH)4(C4H5O2)12 are discussed chiefly through reaction mechanisms without condition-specific numerical lithography performance. No invented performance records were added.
Organic CAR/n-CAR, molecular-glass and HSQ results in sections 2.1–2.4 were not expanded into records because this extraction targets metal-oxo and metal-organic materials.

No experimental metal-oxo/metal-organic resist composition, coated-film structure, lithographic dose–size pair, tone, contrast, LER/LWR, film thickness, substrate, bake or development conditions is reported. Electron-pulse doses describe solution radiolysis, and the introductory 11 nm half-pitch is a requirements discussion rather than an achieved pattern.

No material-specific resist EUV absorption, etch performance, surface roughness, thickness loss or film stability is reported; transient optical absorption and radical-ion lifetimes concern dissolved model ligands.
Reviewed supplied article text MAIN:p1–MAIN:p7 and selected page images MAIN:p2–MAIN:p7 only. No supplementary files were acquired, and other page or figure pixels were not reviewed.

The supplied MAIN:p1–MAIN:p45 text reports no identifiable resist formulation or condition-specific lithography results: exposure dose, pattern size, tone, contrast, LER/LWR, film thickness, substrate, bake and development conditions are absent. No resist-specific absorption, etch performance, roughness, thickness loss or stability results are reported.
Visual review was limited to supplied images MAIN:p3, MAIN:p10, MAIN:p36 and MAIN:p41–MAIN:p45. Other page and figure pixels were not supplied or visually reviewed.
No supplementary files were acquired or reviewed. The cited polysilane photoresist publications were not supplied; their material identities and performance cannot be inferred from reference entries.
